*Functions* 
- Function to replace "<LOD" with 0.5 LOD-value
- Function to set number of digits
- Function for statistics in plotting
```{r functions}
#function to recognize "<LOD" and to replace with 0.5*LOD. 
dLimity <- function(v){
  v <- as.character(v)
  isLimit <- grepl("<", v)  #grepl() is a built-in R function looks for a smaller string of characters
  v[isLimit] <- as.numeric(gsub("<(.*)", "\\1", v[isLimit]))/2 #gsub(pattern, replacement, x) for substitution
  as.numeric(v)}

#Test to set desired number of digits
sigfig <- function(vec, digits){
  return(gsub("\\.$", "", formatC(signif(vec,digits=digits), digits=digits, format="fg", flag="#")))}

#For statistics plotting (not used?)
get_box_stats <- function(y, upper_limit = max(df$mpg) * 1.15) {
  return(data.frame(
    y = 0.95 * upper_limit,
    label = paste(
      "n =", length(y), "\n")))}
```

## Make heatmap table based on sample types and category
```{r preparations for heatmap}
df3 <- subset(df2x, !is.na(value)) #nothing removed

df4_freq = df3 %>% #calculate detection frequency
  group_by(Medium_id, compound, Site_Category) %>% #include site category depending on analysis 
  mutate(lodcount = sum(lengths(regmatches(value, gregexpr("<", value)))), 
            n = (length(value)),
            det_frac = (100-(lodcount/n)*100))%>%
  ungroup() 

#avoid plotting zeroes
df4_filt <- df4_freq %>%  #zeroes assigned <LOD
  mutate(plotting = ifelse(det_frac == 0, #there are no zeroes here
                           "<LOD", 
                           value))

# claculate 0.5xLOD 
df4_filt_X <- cbind(df4_filt[,c(1:24)], apply(df4_filt[,25, drop=F],2, dLimity))

#calcualte means
df4_finalx = df4_filt_X %>%
  group_by(Medium_id, compound, Site_Category) %>%
  mutate(meanx = mean(plotting, na.rm = TRUE))%>% 
  ungroup()
```

Test skewness
Generally, a skewness value between -1 and +1 is considered acceptably close to symmetric/normal for many statistical purposes. Values beyond -2 and +2 suggest substantial non-normality. 
 Log transformation is warranted for right-skewed data (positive skew)
```{r test skewness}
library(moments)
sapply(corry, moments::skewness)

par(mfrow = c(2, 3))   # adjust layout for multiple plots
for (col in names(corry)) {
  hist(corry[[col]], main = col, xlab = "", col = "lightblue")
}

#density plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
for (col in names(corry)) {
  plot(density(corry[[col]], na.rm = TRUE), main = col, col = "darkgreen")
}

boxplot(corry, main = "Boxplots of variables", col = "lightgreen")

```
log-transform
```{r}
corry1 <- corry %>%
  mutate(across(c(1:12, 14), ~ log(.x), .names = "{col}_log"))
```

#Figure 4 - PCA
We scaled the supplementary variables by multiplying their coordinates with a constant so their arrow lengths match the scale used for the active variables in the biplot.
This was needed because fviz_pca_biplot() automatically rescales active variables to fit the spread of the data, while supplementary variables are left unscaled and therefore appear artificially short unless adjusted.
https://f0nzie.github.io/machine_learning_compilation/detailed-study-of-principal-component-analysis.html
```{r PCA}
# Run PCA on the active variables only; add phys-chem as supplementary
corry2 <- corry1[,c(13, 15, 28, 16:27)]

#PCA
#replace names to make nicer plots
print(colnames(corry2))
corry3 <- corry2 %>% 
  rename("Henry's law constant" = "HENRYS_LAW_ATM.M3.MOLE_OPERA_PRED_log", 
         "Octanol-water part." = "OCTANOL_WATER_PARTITION_LOGP_OPERA_PRED",
        "Molar mass" = "AVERAGE_MASS",
        "Water_Football"= "Water (ng/L)_Artificial football field_log",
        "Sludge_WWTP" ="Sludge (ng/g, d.w.)_Wastewater treatment plant_log",
        "Sediment_River"="Sediment (ng/g, d.w.)_Urban river_log",
        "Water_Road"="Water (ng/L)_Road environment_log",
        "Sediment_Pond"="Sediment (ng/g, d.w.)_Urban pond_log",
        "PM10_Park" ="PM10 (ng/m^3)_Urban park_log",
        "Sludge_Football" ="Sludge (ng/g, d.w.)_Artificial football field_log",
        "Water_WWTP"="Water (ng/L)_Wastewater treatment plant_log",
        "Water_River"="Water (ng/L)_Urban river_log",
        "Sludge_Road"="Sludge (ng/g, d.w.)_Road environment_log",
        "Water_Pond"="Water (ng/L)_Urban pond_log",
        "PM10_Road"="PM10 (ng/m^3)_Road environment_log"
        )

rownames(corry3) <- c("2-OHBT", "6PPD", "6PPD-Q", "ABT", "BTSA", "DPG", "DPPD", "HMMM", "IPPD", "MBT", "MTBT", "PhBT", "TMQ")

colnames(corry3)[colnames(corry3) == "Henry's law constant"] <- "Henry's law const." #shorter name for plot

res.pca <- PCA(corry3,
  scale.unit = TRUE,
  graph = FALSE,
  quanti.sup = c(1:3))    # <- physiochemical variables as supplementary)

summary(res.pca)

# Extract coordinates
ind <- res.pca$ind$coord
var <- res.pca$var$coord
sup <- res.pca$quanti.sup$coord

# Compute scaling
scale_factor <- min(
  (max(ind[,1]) - min(ind[,1])) / (max(var[,1]) - min(var[,1])),
  (max(ind[,2]) - min(ind[,2])) / (max(var[,2]) - min(var[,2]))
)

# Apply to supplementary variables
sup_scaled <- sup * scale_factor

# Biplot: active variable loadings + supplementary (phys-chem) arrows in red
p <- fviz_pca_biplot(res.pca,
  invisible = "quanti.sup",
  repel = TRUE,
  col.var = "dodgerblue4",         # active variables (blue)
  #col.quanti.sup = "firebrick",  # phys-chem arrows (red)
  col.ind = "#333333",  # Individuals color
  label = "all",
  labelsize =4.5)                  # show loading labels

sup_scaled <- res.pca$quanti.sup$coord * 3.5   # try 3-5

#align label with arrow head
# scale arrows correctly
fviz_add(p, sup_scaled,
         geom = c("arrow", "text"),
         color = "firebrick",
         linetype = "dashed",
         labelsize =4.5)+
  theme(
  axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
  plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face="bold"))

ggsave("PCA_biplot.png", bi, width = 8.5, height = 7.5)


fviz_pca_ind(pca_result,
             col.ind = "cos2", # Color by the quality of representation
             gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"),
             repel = TRUE     # Avoid text overlapping
             )

fviz_pca_var(pca_result,
             col.var = "contrib", # Color by contributions to the PC
             gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"),
             repel = TRUE     # Avoid text overlapping
                 )

fviz_screeplot(res.pca)
# variable contributions on axis 1
fviz_contrib(res.pca, choice="var", axes = 1, top = 10 )
# variable contributions on axis 1
fviz_contrib(res.pca, choice="var", axes = 2, top = 10 )

res.desc <- dimdesc(res.pca, axes = c(1,2), proba = 0.05)
res.desc$Dim.1

var <- get_pca_var(res.pca)

# Loadings/coordinates of variables on PC1 & PC2
round(var$coord[, 1:2], 3)

# Contributions (%) of variables to PC1 & PC2
round(var$contrib[, 1:2], 2)

# Quality of representation (cos�) of variables on PC1 & PC2
round(var$cos2[, 1:2], 3)

var <- get_pca_var(res.pca)

load_tbl <- data.frame(
  Variable        = rownames(var$coord),
  PC1_loading     = var$coord[, 1],
  PC2_loading     = var$coord[, 2],
  PC1_contrib_pct = var$contrib[, 1],
  PC2_contrib_pct = var$contrib[, 2],
  PC1_cos2        = var$cos2[, 1],
  PC2_cos2        = var$cos2[, 2],
  row.names = NULL
)

# Round numeric columns
load_tbl[] <- lapply(load_tbl, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) round(x, 3) else x)
head(load_tbl)
```
